prompt: A smart speaker keeps users' voice recordings to improve its model without asking them first.
why: Using personal data without consent is a privacy issue.
trap: Telling users afterward would be transparency; the missing consent is privacy.

prompt: A chatbot fine-tuned on support tickets sometimes repeats customers' home addresses to other users.
tells: repeats customers' home addresses to other users
why: Exposing personal data is a privacy and security failure.
trap: It's not harmful content in the hate or violence sense; it's leaked personal data.

prompt: Only the HR team should be able to query the model that was trained on employee salary records.
tells: Only the HR team should be able to query
why: Controlling who can access sensitive data is privacy and security.
trap: Accountability is about responsibility for outcomes, not access rights.

prompt: Attackers try to trick an assistant into revealing confidential files it can read on the company network.
why: Resisting attacks that expose data is security.
trap: Content filters can help detect the attack, but the principle at stake is privacy and security.

prompt: Before training a model on patient records, the team removes names and replaces exact birthdates with age ranges.
tells: removes names and replaces exact birthdates
why: Protecting personal data in training is privacy and security.
trap: PII detection is a tool that could do this; the principle asked about is privacy.

prompt: Users must be able to ask for their chat history to be deleted and excluded from any future training.
why: Giving people control over their data is privacy.
trap: Telling users what you do with data is transparency; letting them delete it is privacy.

prompt: Customer documents uploaded to an AI app must be encrypted and kept only in the company's own storage.
why: Protecting data at rest and controlling where it lives is privacy and security.
trap: Data zones control processing location; encryption and storage are privacy controls.

prompt: A store wants to recognize returning shoppers by face. Lawyers insist shoppers must opt in first.
why: Consent before using biometric data is privacy.
trap: Telling shoppers is transparency; needing their agreement is privacy.
